item.title: Daily melt pond and net ice surface fractions in the Arctic Ocean from MODIS visible imagery: 2000–2024
item.description:
Daily melt pond and net ice surface fractions in the Arctic Ocean from MODIS visible imagery: 2000–2024
Remon Sadikni and Stefan Kern
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8537–8568, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8537-2026, 2026
Melt ponds form during summer on Arctic sea ice. They impact the amount of solar energy entering the sea ice-ocean system. We describe the retrieval method of a new data set of the daily melt-pond coverage on Arctic sea ice north of 60 degrees latitude North for June to August of years 2000 to 2024 based on satellite remote sensing. The results of the quality assessment against independent observations demonstrate the data set’s credibility and usefulness for Arctic climate system studies.

item.title: DigiSylva: a plot-level dataset of forest attributes integrating field and airborne laser scanning measurements across the boreal-temperate ecotone of the northeastern United States
item.description:
DigiSylva: a plot-level dataset of forest attributes integrating field and airborne laser scanning measurements across the boreal-temperate ecotone of the northeastern United States
Xinyuan Wei, Daniel Hayes, Lei Ma, Jianheng Zhao, Grant Daniels, Joanne White, Archibald Owen, David Sandilands, Shambhu Katel, Chenye Zhang, George Hurtt, and Aaron Weiskittel
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-773,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Mapping and monitoring forests needs ground-measured trees matched with aircraft laser scans, but such public data are rare in the northeastern United States. We measured 6,137 trees on 308 plots in five Maine forests, located each plot within one meter, collected new aircraft scans in 2025 and 2026, and matched the plots with scans since 2010 and aerial and satellite images. This free dataset helps map forest carbon and track forest change.

item.title: Crop-specific manure nitrogen and phosphorus management in US croplands from 1970 to 2025
item.description:
Crop-specific manure nitrogen and phosphorus management in US croplands from 1970 to 2025
Peiyu Cao, Bo Yi, and Chaoqun Lu
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-835,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Manure supplies organic nitrogen and phosphorus to cropland, but existing estimates overlook livestock herd dynamics and aross-crop variations in the United States. We combined livestock records, farm surveys, and crop maps to reconstruct manure production and management. Our dataset maps manure nutirent production and crop-specific application rates, timing, and methods from 1970 to 2025. These findings support better nutrient management and water pollution reduction.

item.title: Nitrogen budgets for eight major arable crops in European countries for 1961–2019
item.description:
Nitrogen budgets for eight major arable crops in European countries for 1961–2019
Hongyu Lin, Hans J. M. van Grinsven, Rasmus Einarsson, Minghua Zhou, Deepak Ray, Alfredo Rodríguez, João Serra, Eduardo Aguilera, Alberto Sanz-Cobena, Miguel Quemada, Sergiy Medinets, Arthur Beusen, and Luis Lassaletta
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-891,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
The common policy indicator for nitrogen (N) pollution from arable land is the national N surplus, which is the difference between all inputs and the output in crop harvest. Currently published N surpluses are lumped values for arable land and provide no insight into the contributions from different crops. We quantified surpluses for eight major crops using novel approaches for manure N input and harvest N. While root crops have the highest N surplus per ha, cereals dominate N surplus mass.

item.title: Twenty Years of data from the RAPID-MOCHA-WBTS array: Long-Term Changes in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, Heat and Freshwater Transports
item.description:
Twenty Years of data from the RAPID-MOCHA-WBTS array: Long-Term Changes in the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, Heat and Freshwater Transports
Tillys Petit, Shane Elipot, David A. Smeed, William E. Johns, Ryan H. Smith, Denis L. Volkov, Brian A. King, Elaine L. McDonagh, Darren Rayner, Julie Collins, Adam Ward, and Ben I. Moat
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-922,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
For over 20 years, measurements across the Atlantic at 26° N has continuously recorded the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation that carry heat northward and help shape the climate. This paper describes the resulting data, how they are produced and shared, and how they show changes in these ocean circulation over time. It also releases the computer code used to produce them, so anyone can reproduce and reuse the data.
